messages.author: fa8b9dad524607ca
messages.subject: Shiny & Reproducible Research
parts:
Thank you Joe and Winston, everyone else who may be on the shiny team, as well as the rest of the contributors in this group, my project has progressed much further in one month than I had anticipated in large part due to shiny and all of your support.

My next largest concern, which I have not yet come to an elegant solution for, is a matter of reproducible research.  It all boils down to being able to track the user and be able to follow their steps to produce the same results.  The issues that have come up are 1) The code used for shiny would have to be manually altered to get rid of shiny specific functions and mechanics in order to run through as an R script (I presume?),  2) The user is likely to want to save multiple plots generated with each plot function with the shiny program, so simply using the last available reactives and inputs$s will not suffice,  3) The user inputs are not likely to be linearly performed (user goes through steps 1-7, decides to change something in step 4 and continues from that point forward again) and 4) the R history saved appears to just be the runApp() function, at least when run locally.

The practical reasons for needing reproducibility could be as simple as a collaborator comes to me and says "I made this plot yesterday with the application you made, I think I used the following criteria, could you please make it again with the following custom changes to it?" or "I made this plot a couple months ago, and I performed some independent validation and would like to publish it- could you provide the code used to produce it for the supplemental portion?"

So I figured I would check in to see if anyone else had given thought to the above, and if the shiny team had anything in the works (or even draftboard/to-do list) related to these issues.  The ugly solution I had come up with was to create a list of lists that will be appended each time an action button is clicked- named after the action button pressed and the time/date when it was pressed, including the list of input$s, reactives and their contents, and upon saving a plot, the relevant list will too be saved.  And at the end, the list of lists (stalking everything they did) would also be saved.  These could be used to be input the shiny application manually again, or an R script could be mocked up to mimic the shiny application, minus the reactives, isolates, action buttons, overlapping object names and etc, implementing the saved input$s and reactives.  I would love to hear a better solution.

Thanks again,
Mike

Mike

I asked something related a while back:

"Is it likely Shiny will have a feature where you can (1) save the input-object directly to a file and (2) load it back-in with a button click? The next time you use your shiny app, input you could replaced it with the previous state."

in this thread a few months ago: 

https://groups.google.com/forum/?fromgroups#!searchin/shiny-discuss/save$20input/shiny-discuss/Olr8m0JwMTo/ZzdOPIrW_MoJ

Not sure it there have been any updates. Alex has a nice approach that used elements in a url. If you have a LOT of inputs that might get messy I assume.
